intent: A single compact action positioned in the alert's top-right corner - something the user can do right there without leaving the page.
typical_uses: One button (or icon button) that responds directly to what the alert reports (retry, dismiss, view details)

dont_use_when.situation: More than one action, or an action that needs more room than a corner-positioned control

instead.target: a custom layout inside AlertDescription, or a heavier surface entirely for anything beyond one compact control
instead.note: AlertAction reserves a fixed amount of padding sized for a single control; this kit has no dedicated multi-action row component for inside an Alert today.

invariants.text: AlertAction always renders absolutely positioned in its nearest Alert's top-right corner; it does not take part in the normal document flow beside the title and description text.

anti_patterns.dont: Put more than one interactive control inside AlertAction expecting them to lay out side by side
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep AlertAction to a single compact control - its fixed corner position and the padding Alert reserves for it are both sized for one

good.title: A single retry button in the corner
good.code:
<Alert variant="destructive">
  <AlertTitle>Payment failed</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>We couldn't charge your card ending in 4242.</AlertDescription>
  <AlertAction>
    <Button size="sm" variant="outline">Retry</Button>
  </AlertAction>
</Alert>

bad.title: Two actions crammed into one AlertAction
bad.why: AlertAction reserves a fixed amount of corner padding sized for one compact control; a second button overflows or overlaps it instead of laying out side by side.
